deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss's Ceres work of Dec 1805 to Jan 1806. He compares meridian observations (Seeberg/Gotha, Milan, Paris) with an ephemeris, then starts a new orbit computation. This page does four things.

(A) TOP: geocentric places for the two Dec 29 observations (9h37m and 13h15m, from the previous page), one column each.
- Heliocentric equatorial coordinates have the form x_i = A_i sin(E + K_i) + c_i, with log A = 0.4346953, 0.3997142, 0.1008078. The logs 9.4180676, 9.9732603, 9.9974554 (and 9.4190291, ...) are log|sin(E+K_i)|. The constants c = (+0.1820815, -0.0993061, -0.0838776) are the -a e P_i terms.
- This gives (x,y,z) = (-0.7124641+0.1820815, ...) = (-0.5303826, +2.2610336, +1.1700233).
- The Sun's geocentric coordinates (X,Y,Z) = (+0.1334946, -0.8935200, -0.3878680) are added. Their norm is about 0.983 = R.
- Small corrections (-151, -251, -297 in units of the 7th decimal) follow. These are probably light-time/aberration or equinox reduction (my interpretation).
- Result: xi = -0.3969031, eta = +1.3674885, zeta = +0.7821256.
- Reduction to RA and Dec:
  - log eta = 0.1359237, log|xi| = 9.5986845, so tan(alpha) = eta/xi with xi < 0, giving alpha in the 2nd quadrant: alpha = 106 deg 11' 5.88".
  - log sin(alpha) = 9.9824372; log(rho cos delta) = log eta - log sin(alpha) = 0.1534865.
  - log zeta = 9.8932765; tan(delta) = zeta/(rho cos delta), so delta = 28 deg 46' 44.84".
  - log cos(delta) = 9.9427440; log rho = 0.2107425.
  - The second column similarly gives alpha = 106 deg 8' 44.35", delta = 28 deg 47' 38.18".
  - 2.6875 is a constant log (probably light-time related; unsure).
- Errors (ephemeris minus observation): -23.62", -13.76" and -39.15", -13.62".

(B) ERRORES table for Dec 29 (twice), Dec 31, Jan 3, 4, 5, 7, 12 (all except Jan 3 are computed on the previous page).
- Group means in RA: first four = -35.8725", last four = -35.3550".
- Group means in Dec: first four = -13.9200", last four = -15.3250".
- 'Error normalis' is set to RA -35.48", Dec -15.18". This is not the plain mean of all eight (that would be -35.61", -14.62"). Its derivation is not shown.

(C) JANUARY 3 COMPUTATION.
- Time: Seeberg 12h26m29s minus 33m35s (longitude difference) = Paris 11h52m54s = 11.881666h, so t = Jan 3.49506944.
- Mean motion: log t + log n = 0.5434558 + 2.8863074 (n about 769.65"/day), so n t = 2690.07" = 44'50.07".
- Mean anomaly: M = 322 deg 35' 52.43" (epoch) + 44'50.07" = 323 deg 20' 42.50".
- Kepler's equation E - e'' sin E = M, with log e'' = 4.2216648 (e about 0.0808 expressed in arcseconds) and log|sin E| = 9.8044738 (sin E < 0). This gives e sin E = -2 deg 57' 0.35", so E = 320 deg 23' 42.15".
- Arguments E + K_i: 196 deg 20' 51.00", 111 deg 4' 2.48", 84 deg 58' 14.84". The differences 85 deg 16' 48.52" and 26 deg 5' 47.64" are the same as on Jan 5.
- log sin of these: 9.4494203, 9.9699554, 9.9983248.
- Heliocentric coordinates: (-0.7658004+0.1820815, 2.3424460-0.0993061, 1.2564136-0.0838776) = (-0.5837189, 2.2431399, 1.1725360).
- Sun: (+0.2215680, -0.8786702, -0.3814219). Geocentric: xi = -0.3621509, eta = 1.3644697, zeta = 0.7911141.
- Logs: 0.1349639, 9.5588896, giving alpha = 104 deg 51' 52.02"; log sin(alpha) = 9.9852178; log zeta = 9.8982392; log(rho cos delta) = 0.1497461; delta = 29 deg 15' 57.55"; log cos(delta) = 9.9406955; log rho = 0.2090506.
- 'corrig.': 104 deg 52' 27.50", 29 deg 16' 12.73". This is the computed place minus the error normalis (+35.48", +15.18"), i.e. a corrected (normal) place for Jan 3.

(D) SOLAR PLACE FOR JAN 3 from tables of the Delambre/von Zach type.
- Mean longitude: 9s 9 deg 25' 47.31" + 3 deg 26' 59.15" + 1' 5.25" = 282 deg 53' 51.71".
- Anomaly argument: 4995.59 + 95.82 + 0.50 = 5091.91.
- Equation of centre +6' 48.37" and -0.07" give 283 deg 0' 40.01".
- Perturbation and table corrections +1.55, +3.21, +3.79, +37.86 give 283 deg 1' 26.42". This value is the one used for X, Y, Z.
- Arguments I to X, Omega, sun-symbol updated (348+119 = 467, etc.); XI to XXI are listed.
- Two columns of small terms sum to 6.46 and 5.38.
- Apparent solar longitude: 283 deg 1' 9.64" (about -16.78" from the previous value, presumably aberration plus nutation; my interpretation).
- Radius vector: 0.9832377 + 27 - 359 - 57 - 220 = 0.9831768, then +61. log R = 9.9926343 (9.9926316 before the correction).
- Obliquity: 23 deg 27' 53.53" + 1.20 + 0.27 = 23 deg 27' 55.00".
- Logs: cos(sun) = 9.3528754; R cos(eps) = 9.9551440; |sin(sun)| = 9.9886819; R sin(eps) = 9.5927238.
- Hence X = R cos(sun), Y = R cos(eps) sin(sun), Z = R sin(eps) sin(sun). These reproduce (0.2215680, -0.8786702, -0.3814219).
- Solar latitude: -0.10 - 0.11 + 0.09 + 0.14 = +0.02".
- Check lines compare the solar values at the Paris-reduced and Seeberg times: 103 deg 1' 9.32" or 9.64" or 9.38"; 6.28.32.38 (unidentified); log R = 9.9926343.

(E) SCRAPS AND 'Neue Rechnung der Ceres 1806'.
- Log summations, e.g. 9.9972203 + 0.0593223 + 0.0034835 = 0.0600261.
- Start of a new orbit determination for Ceres. log r = 0.428017 and 0.406327 (r about 2.680, 2.549) and the angle 2f = 62 deg 55' 41.4" = 2 x 31 deg 27' 50.7" appear.
- The next page continues with f = 15 deg 43' 55.35", so this is the determination of elements from two radii vectors, the included angle and the time.
- Time interval perhaps 116.84722 days (uncertain).
- The lower-right numbers are too fragmentary to reconstruct fully.
errors: No arithmetic slips found in the checked lines: the Dec 29 reductions, the error means, the Jan 3 Kepler step, the coordinate sums, the RA/Dec reductions, the solar longitude and obliquity sums, and the radius-vector sum.
The two Dec 29 RA errors (-23.62" vs -39.15", same night) disagree by about 15". This points to an observational problem rather than a computational one.

'Error normalis' (-35.48", -15.18") is not the arithmetic mean of the tabulated errors (-35.61", -14.62"), nor a simple mean of the two group means. It was presumably obtained by weighting, selection or an earlier computation not shown here.

The angle written (as transcribed) as 196 deg 26' 51.00" must be 196 deg 20' 51.00". This follows both from its log sine 9.4494203 and from the constant difference 85 deg 16' 48.52" with the next argument (as on Jan 5). So either the transcription or Gauss's figure is off by 6'; the log used is correct.

results.what: Geocentric RA/Dec of Ceres from orbital elements via the coordinate forms x_i = A_i sin(E+K_i) + c_i plus solar coordinates, with Kepler's equation solved for E
results.modern_name: Ephemeris computation using Gaussian vectorial (equatorial) constants
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria Motus 1809; used in his Ceres ephemerides 1801-1806)

results.what: Comparison of observation and ephemeris; mean errors over groups of observations; correction of a computed place by a mean error to obtain a 'normal' place
results.modern_name: Residuals (O-C) and normal places for orbit improvement
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 18th-19th c. astronomers; normal places systematized by Gauss and his contemporaries

results.what: Solar longitude, radius vector and obliquity from solar tables with perturbation arguments, converted to equatorial X,Y,Z
results.modern_name: Solar ephemeris from tables (Delambre / von Zach)

results.what: Beginning of a new Ceres orbit from two radii vectors (log r = 0.428017, 0.406327), included angle 2f = 62 deg 55' 41.4" and time interval
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria Motus 1809, Bk I Sec III)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine working material from Gauss's well-documented Ceres ephemeris comparisons and orbit corrections of 1805-06. The only point of interest is the documentation of how a corrected 'normal place' was formed.

transcription_corrections: 'Paris 52,9 = 11h 38' 1666' should read Paris 11h52'54" = 11,881666 hours (Seeberg 12h26'29" minus 33'35"), giving Jan 3.49506944.
'196°26'51,00' is 196°20'51,00 on numerical grounds (log sin = 9.4494203; argument differences match Jan 5).
The perturbation column total read '+4,08' is probably '+1,08' (= 6.46 - 5.38).
The column headings 'I III V VII IX X Omega sun' are tabular arguments; the right-hand column of small terms sums to 5.38 (signs as written, with 2.84 contributing positively in that total).
